51272678.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His6 tagged human TEAD4-YBD (217 to 434 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli C43 (DE3) cells by SPR analysis
51272678.references_previous: Y.L. Wang, L.J. Li, B.D. Zhang, J. Xing, S.J. Chen, W. Wan, Y.K. Song, H. Jiang, H.L. Jiang, J. Luo, M.Y. Zheng, Discovery of novel disruptor of silencing telomeric 1-like (DOT1L) inhibitors using a target-specific scoring function for the (S)-Adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-Dependent methyltransferase family, J. Med. Chem. 60 (2017) 2026–2036.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.6. Surface pla: The SPR experiments were performed at 25 °C on Biacore T200 instruments (GE Healthcare) as previously described [45]. hTEAD4-YBD protein (217–434) was directly immobilized onto the CM5 biosensor chip to a level of 3,500 response unit using the standard amine coupling approach. Binding kinetic measurements were conducted in the running buffer (25 mM Hepes 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% P20, 0.2% DMSO). Data was processed using Biacore T200 Evaluation software to calculate the equilibrium dissociation constant.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. Biochemical and biophysical methods demonstrated the direct binding of DC-TEADin01. (A) The protein thermal shift assays. Synthetic YAP peptide was used as the positive control with the ratio of 1:5. (B–C) CPMG and STD NMR spectrum assays. (D) Competitive NMR binding assay using 1 μM palmitoyl CoA. (E) SPR assays. (F) The predicted binding mode of DC-TEADin01 with TEAD4-YBD in molecular docking studies.
original_paragraph.Figure 2E: The SPR sensorgram in Figure 2E shows the response unit (RU) over time (s) for DC-TEADin01 binding to TEAD4-YBD. The concentrations tested are labeled on the right: 100, 67, 44, 30, 20, 13, 9, 6, and 4 μM. The graph shows the association phase (0 to ~100 s) and dissociation phase (~100 to 200 s). The inset text indicates 'TEAD4-YBD Kd = 41 μM'.

assay_conditions.running_buffer_composition: 25 mM Hepes 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% P20, 0.2% DMSO
